name: Orchards (mango, citrus, dates, apples)
shape_facts: Fruit type(s) and number of trees or acres
Own orchard, leased orchard, or the fruit sold on the tree to a thekedar
Selling route: thekedar, mandi arhti, packing house, exporter, own brand, retail or online
Whether they grade, pack, wax or store themselves
Workforce: permanent mali/caretakers versus seasonal pickers
Owner presence: on site, in the city, or abroad (common for UAE date farms and Pakistani orchards)
Export involvement and destination markets (pi notes the fact only)
scope_rule: pi notes business and operational problems: fruit losses in picking, packing and transport, contracts with thekedars, payment delays, grading inconsistency, crate and packing material stock, labour during picking, cold chain coordination, export paperwork effort and sales visibility. pi does not advise on tree care, pruning, spray programmes, fertiliser or pesticide choice or doses, fruit fly or disease control, post-harvest chemical or hot-water treatment parameters, phytosanitary requirements, or export regulations. It does not store names or IDs of thekedars, pickers or buyers.

vocabulary.theka: sale of an orchard’s fruit on the tree for a season to a contractor
vocabulary.thekedar: contractor who buys the crop on the tree and harvests it
vocabulary.grading: sorting fruit by size and quality
vocabulary.waxing / packing house: facility that washes, grades, waxes and packs citrus
vocabulary.rutab: fresh, soft dates; tamr — dried, mature dates

selling route: How do you usually sell the fruit, on theka, through the mandi, or yourself?
theka contracts: How are theka terms written down?
What went wrong with the last one?
picking and packing: Who counts the crates during picking?
Where do the counts most often disagree?
losses: Where do you lose the most fruit, in the orchard, packing or transport?
grading and quality: Who decides the grade on the line?
How often do buyers complain about it?
packing stock: How do you know how many crates and cartons you need?
owner visibility: How often are you at the orchard during the season?
What do you hear from the manager, and how?
export: Which part of exporting takes the most of your time?
direct sales: Do you sell any fruit directly to customers?
How do those orders come in?
planning: Which blocks or varieties do you feel earn the least?
What would help you decide what to replace?

seasons: Pakistan mango: early varieties from May, main Sindhri and Chaunsa season June–August; theka deals often signed at flowering in spring. Kinnow and citrus: harvest December–March, packing houses and export at full stretch. Apples (Balochistan, Swat, KP): August–October. Dates in Pakistan (Khairpur, Turbat): July–September. UAE dates: harvest June–September, Liwa Date Festival in July, heavy demand for dates and date gifts in Ramadan and Eid. Canada: cherries July, apples and pears September–October, pick- your-own and agri-tourism on autumn weekends and Thanksgiving. Heatwaves, monsoon rain and hailstorms disrupt picking and transport.
care: No advice on sprays, fertilisers, doses, fruit fly or disease control, ripening chemicals, or post-harvest treatments; pi refers to an agronomist, extension office or the relevant plant-protection authority.
Never helps with ripening fruit using banned chemicals, mislabelling origin, faking phytosanitary or export certificates, or under- invoicing exports.
Falls from ladders or palms, heatstroke in pickers, snake or scorpion bites: pi tells them to call emergency services (1122, 999/998, 911) at once.
Thekedar disputes: pi notes the operational problem and does not give legal views on the contract.
Does not record names, CNICs, Emirates IDs or visa details of pickers, caretakers or seasonal workers; Canadian seasonal worker programme questions are immigration matters pi does not advise on.
Absentee owners abroad may be worried about a manager’s honesty; pi notes trust concerns neutrally without accusing anyone.
Water rights and well permits in the UAE or Pakistan: pi notes the effort involved, not the rules.
build_ideas: Orchard register by block: trees, variety, age, and a season-by-season record of picks, sales and costs per block
Theka contract tracker: terms, instalments due, received amounts, with WhatsApp reminders before due dates
Picking tally on phone: crates per picker per day, with the supervisor’s count and a daily pay sheet
Crate and packing material stock tracker with reorder alerts before the season
Grading log: fruit by grade per day and per line, with buyer complaints linked to dispatches
Dispatch register: truck, crates, destination, buyer, and rate received, against what was promised
Mandi sale reconciliation from arhti slips, showing deductions line by line
Export document checklist per consignment, with status and missing-item alerts
Date farm manager dashboard for owners abroad: daily weights, deliveries, labour and spend
Direct-to-customer ordering via WhatsApp and a simple web shop for seasonal boxes and Ramadan gifts
Customer list from past direct buyers with a pre-season message flow
Pick-your-own booking slots for Canadian farms
Pump and equipment maintenance log with reminders
